open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct actual DQM paths whose score span is the full annihilator of the three normal classes on the unrestricted saturated fixed-defect joint-solvability germ, or exhibit a counterexample inside that same full germ.
open_obligations.obstruction: The declared closed-range and operator-continuity conditions yield continuous moving kernel and cokernel projections but neither differentiable projection lifts nor a locally surjective constant-rank parameterization of the intersection of the outcome- and treatment-solvability loci. First-order annihilation therefore does not by itself integrate to an admissible path.
open_obligations.attempted: I reduced the proposed lifting argument to a constant-rank parameterization of the coupled incidence set and checked what the operator perturbation lemma actually supplies along DQM paths. Its conclusion is only continuity with an unspecified modulus, so the needed derivative cannot be inferred. The regular finite chart, singular two-branch chart, and transverse different-row-space chart remain valid positive tests, but none supplies the missing unrestricted Hilbert parameterization.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved finite-dimensional calculations establish reverse lifting on three strictly positive germs: the regular \(36\)-cell rank-two germ, the singular two-branch \(3\)-by-\(3\) germ, and the transverse \(4\)-by-\(4\) rank-two germ with different arm row spaces. They also establish that an arbitrary singleton subchart has tangent space \(\{0\}\), so chart saturation is necessary.

For the general germ, the available operator argument stops strictly before path realization. Indeed, along a DQM path \(P_t\), DQM gives \(H(P_t,P)=O(|t|)\). The transported-operator continuity assumption and the kernel perturbation lemma imply only
\[
\left\|\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\vee
\left\|\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=o(1).
\]
No declared assumption supplies an \(O(|t|)\) modulus, a derivative of either projection, or a locally surjective constant-rank parameterization of the intersection
\[
\mathcal U_P\cap\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}}(P)\cap
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{trt}}(P).
\]
Consequently, annihilation of the three displayed first-order normal classes cannot presently be integrated into an actual curve in that intersection. The finite incidence parameterizations prove the desired equality on their stated finite germs, but do not imply the unrestricted Hilbert-space equality.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove bridge-score pathwise validity and the claimed pathwise-differentiability if-and-only-if statement on the unbounded existence-only chart, in addition to resolving reverse score lifting.
open_obligations.obstruction: Separate square integrability of the bridges and outcome does not control the products required to differentiate a bridge score along every DQM path. Operator continuity has no first-order modulus, so continuity of nearby minimum-norm representatives does not make the exact doubly robust product remainder little-o of the path parameter. Pathwise differentiability also does not presently imply that a single bridge-pair score belongs to square-integrable space.
open_obligations.attempted: I used the exact nearby-law doubly robust remainder and continuous pseudoinverse/kernel perturbation. The remainder is a product of a nearby primal and dual change; the assumptions make those changes continuous but do not provide the rate or product integrability needed after division by the path parameter. The remaining Hilbert projection argument was completed conditionally and is recorded below.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The Hilbert-space conclusion is complete under the two missing analytic premises. Namely, suppose that
\(\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp\) and that some
\(\phi_0\in\Phi_P\) represents the derivative of \(\theta\) along every actual path score:
\[
\dot\theta_P(s)=E[\phi_0s],\qquad s\in\dot{\mathcal P}_P.
\]
By the proved normal--affine identity and closedness of \(\mathcal C_P\),
\[
\mathcal A_P=\phi_0+\mathcal C_P.
\]
The projection theorem then gives the unique minimum-norm point
\[
\phi_*=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0,
\qquad
\phi_*\perp\mathcal C_P,
\qquad
\phi_*\in\mathcal C_P^\perp=\mathcal T_P.
\]
For every \(s\in\mathcal T_P\),
\[
E[\phi_*s]
=E[\phi_0s]-E[(\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0)s]
=\dot\theta_P(s),
\]
so \(\phi_*\) is the canonical gradient. If \(g\) is any other gradient, then
\(E[(g-\phi_0)s]=0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal T_P\), whence
\(g-\phi_0\in\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal C_P\). Conversely, adding any element of \(\mathcal C_P\) to \(\phi_0\) preserves the derivative representation. Thus the complete gradient set is
\(\phi_0+\mathcal C_P=\mathcal A_P\), and
\[
V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\|\phi_*\|_2^2
=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2].
\]
What is not derived from the frozen assumptions is the premise that a square-integrable bridge score represents every path derivative, nor the converse assertion that pathwise differentiability forces \(\Phi_P\ne\varnothing\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Derive learned-dictionary and population-projection convergence for the displayed same-training-sample ridge construction from primitive, dimension-aware multiplier and Gram-null-space controls.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen fourth-norm bridge rates omit multiplier envelopes needed for cell-signal errors; coordinatewise rates aggregate with a square-root dimension factor in Euclidean vector norm; training--holdout independence does not concentrate a dictionary on its own training sample; and the empirical ridge equation introduces Gram-perturbation and ridge terms multiplied by the learned coefficient envelope in population-null directions.
open_obligations.attempted: I expanded every learned cell signal, aggregated its coordinate errors, and projected the empirical ridge normal equation onto the positive population Gram eigenspace. These calculations verify ridge uniqueness and the four-corner affine identity, while exhibiting the missing multiplier, dimension, dependence, and coefficient-envelope factors explicitly.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Two algebraic parts of the displayed construction are proved. First, since \(\rho_n>0\), every eigenvalue of
\(\widehat G^{(-k)}+\rho_n I\) is at least \(\rho_n\), so the ridge coefficient is unique. Second, direct collection of the pure and four-corner coefficients yields
\[
\sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}=1,
\qquad
\sum_a t_a\sum_{j,\ell}
\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}\widehat S_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}
=\widehat B^{(-k)}-\widehat b^{(-k)\top}
\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}.
\]

The primitive-to-vector rate in the target does not follow from the listed assumptions. For one cell, writing
\(\Delta h=\widehat h-h^0\) and \(\Delta q=\widehat q-q^0\), exact expansion gives
\[
S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)
=(1-I_aq^0)\Delta h+I_a(Y-h^0)\Delta q-I_a\Delta q\Delta h.
\]
The first two terms require fourth-moment envelopes for
\(1-I_aq^0\) and \(I_a(Y-h^0)\), which are not consequences of an envelope on the population dictionary coordinates and \(\phi_0\). Moreover, even if every coordinate error were bounded by a common number \(d_n\), Euclidean aggregation gives only
\[
\|\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}-D^0_{J_n}\|_{L^2(P;\ell^2)}
\le \sqrt{J_n}\,d_n,
\]
not the dimension-free bound asserted in the target.

There is a separate ridge-null-space obstruction. Put
\(G=E[D^0_{J_n}D_{J_n}^{0\top}]\),
\(c=E[D^0_{J_n}B^0]\), and let \(P_R\) project onto
\(\overline{\operatorname{range}}(G)\). Since
\(Gb_{J_n}=c\), the empirical ridge equation implies exactly
\[
G P_R(\widehat b-b_{J_n})
=P_R\{(\widehat c-c)-(\widehat G-G)\widehat b-\rho_n\widehat b\}.
\]
Inverting on the positive eigenspace therefore produces terms proportional to
\(\eta_{c,n}/\kappa_{J_n}\),
\(\eta_{G,n}\|\widehat b\|_2/\kappa_{J_n}\), and
\(\rho_n\|\widehat b\|_2/\kappa_{J_n}\). The affine-weight envelope can at most replace
\(\|\widehat b\|_2\) by a constant multiple of \(L_n\); it does not justify the target's dimension-free
\((\eta_{G,n}+\eta_{c,n})/\kappa_{J_n}\) bound or its ridge term involving only \(\|b_{J_n}\|_2\). Finally, training--holdout independence applies to held-out averages, not to a Gram matrix evaluated on the same training observations used to fit the dictionary. Thus the exact affine identity is valid, but the asserted learned projection convergence remains unproved under the frozen primitive list.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish the foldwise learned efficient-signal convergence and a locally uniform contiguous-path version of all projection and remainder bounds for the explicit estimator.
open_obligations.obstruction: The pointwise cross-fit argument requires the unresolved learned-projection conclusion. Regularity and efficiency additionally require a triangular-array expansion uniform along contiguous joint-chart paths; pointwise primitive-rate assertions do not furnish that uniformity.
open_obligations.attempted: I completed the conditional empirical-process, mixed-bias, i.i.d. central-limit, variance-consistency, and Wald reductions under foldwise efficient-signal convergence. I then checked the claimed contiguous-path step separately and found no declared local-uniform envelopes from which it follows.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The inference reduction is complete once foldwise learned-signal convergence and the stated mixed-bias rate are supplied. Let
\[
f_k=\widehat\psi^{(-k)}-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}.
\]
For fixed \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\), training measurability makes \(f_k\) fixed conditional on \(\mathcal D_{-k}\) when it is evaluated on fold \(k\). Hence, if
\(\max_k\|f_k\|_{L^2(P)}=o_p(1)\), conditional variance gives
\[
\sqrt n\,(P_n-P)f_{k(i)}=o_p(1).
\]
For each affine cell the exact doubly robust remainder can be written in either primal or adjoint form. Cauchy--Schwarz and the affine-weight envelope therefore give
\[
\left|P\widehat\psi^{(-k)}-\theta(P)\right|
\le C L_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},\,r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}
=o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Combining the conditional empirical-process term and this drift yields
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1).
\]
Under i.i.d. sampling and \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), the ordinary i.i.d. central limit theorem gives the stated Gaussian pointwise limit. The same foldwise \(L^2(P)\) convergence, Cauchy--Schwarz, and truncation give
\(\widehat V_n\to_pE[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2]=V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\), hence ratio consistency and pointwise Wald coverage.

This reduction does not supply its premise. The learned-signal convergence is exactly the unresolved conclusion of the preceding lemma. In addition, pointwise \(o_p(1)\) statements under \(P\) do not imply the uniform triangular-array expansion along every contiguous joint-chart path that is needed for regularity and efficiency. Such a conclusion requires locally uniform nuisance, Gram, projection, moment, and remainder controls, none of which is declared by the phrase that the primitive conditions hold along contiguous paths.

prose_updates.tldr: The observed-law model uses the full local \(L^\infty\) likelihood-ratio ball, the full fixed-defect spectrally separated operator stratum, and every DQM curve that remains in both bridge-solvability loci. Reverse score lifting on this unrestricted joint germ remains unresolved: continuous kernel projections do not supply a local parameterization of the coupled solvability intersection. The affine normal identity and all three positive finite tangent tests remain valid, including the exact \(36\)-cell efficiency value \(773723312/334026875\) and strict single-pair nonattainment. The general quotient projection is proved only conditional on both reverse lifting and bridge-score pathwise validity. The displayed learned-projection and Wald claims remain open because the primitive list lacks dimension-aware multiplier, same-training-sample concentration, Gram-null-space, and contiguous-path uniformity controls. The observed bridge functional equals a causal ATE only under the separate latent identification proposition.

project_justification.gap: Existing nonunique-bridge results provide regular inference under additional selection and regularity conditions, but they do not establish the full tangent closure of the simultaneous outcome- and treatment-solvability germ considered here. The present assumptions likewise do not yet turn continuous moving kernels into actual path lifts or certify the growing learned affine projection.
project_justification.niche: The proposed contribution is quotient-tangent efficiency for a saturated fixed-defect observed-law model in which both bridge fibers may be non-singleton. Its distinctive mathematical burden is the coupled score-lifting theorem, including the arms' shared \((W,X)\) marginal, together with an implementable estimator that learns the variance-minimizing affine score.
project_justification.fill: The established contribution currently consists of the affine normal identity, operator-kernel stability, exact finite tangent and nonattainment witnesses, the corrected outcome-only selected-parameter comparison, and conditional Hilbert and cross-fit reductions. General score lifting and primitive-to-Wald inference remain the two load-bearing open steps.

sampling_model.design: The data are dominated and i.i.d. on the canonical full ball \(\mathcal V_P=\{P':\|dP'/dP-1\|_\infty<\varepsilon\}\), intersected with the full transported fixed-nullity, fixed-cokernel, reduced-modulus-separated stratum and both bridge-solvability loci. Every DQM curve remaining in that intersection is admissible; tangent richness is not part of the model definition.
sampling_model.units: The sampling units are \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,Z_i,W_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), independently distributed according to \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment \(A\) is binary. The statistical target is the observed joint-bridge functional; its equality with the ATE uses the separately stated latent consistency, exchangeability, positivity, negative-control, and bridge-compatibility conditions.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-bridge existence is an observed solvability restriction. The main model imposes no injectivity, surjectivity, preferred minimum-norm bridge, or bridge uniqueness.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The fold-indexed penalized-minimax or Galerkin ridge affine ensemble is an explicit candidate estimator. Its ridge uniqueness, affine centering, four-corner conversion, and mixed-bias algebra are valid. The current assumptions do not prove its learned projection rate because multiplier, dimension, training-dependence, coefficient-envelope, and population Gram null-space controls are incomplete.

prose_updates.related_work: Bennett et al. provide penalized bridge inference under additional regularity, while Zhang et al. emphasize nonuniqueness; neither result is identified here with the unresolved global affine-quotient bound. Imbens et al. and Ai--Shan concern uniqueness-restricted or finite-dimensional efficiency regimes and therefore do not establish the two-fiber quotient tangent calculation. Severini--Tripathi is prior art for efficiency of quotient-like functionals, so the new burden is the simultaneous proximal incidence geometry rather than Hilbert projection alone. Ai--Chen and the proximal nuisance-rate literature motivate Galerkin and cross-fit calculations but do not supply the missing same-training-sample and null-space stability bounds for the displayed estimator. The final Bennett publisher theorem text has not been verified here, and no mathematical claim depends on an asserted difference from inaccessible text.
prose_updates.interpretation: With redundant proxies, a chosen bridge pair can define a valid score without minimizing variance over the affine score hull. The exact finite witness proves this phenomenon and supplies a computable variance-minimizing replacement on that germ. For the SUPPORT application, the result is presently a diagnostic and finite-projection prescription: it does not assert that the published proxy specification has nonunique bridges, and the general global-efficiency and Wald guarantees remain conditional on the unresolved lifting and learning steps.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The central unresolved mathematical step is reverse score lifting on the unrestricted saturated infinite-dimensional intersection. Operator-norm continuity gives only continuous kernel projections, not differentiable bridge or kernel selections, a constant-rank chart for the coupled solvability loci, or the product control needed for every unbounded-support path derivative. The learned dictionary claim separately lacks fourth-moment multiplier envelopes, dimension-correct vector aggregation, valid concentration for dictionaries evaluated on their fitting sample, control of empirical ridge leakage through population Gram null directions, and locally uniform contiguous-path rates. Closed range also excludes generic compact infinite-rank inverse problems. Rank-changing unions, general direct-integral measurable charts, and a SUPPORT reanalysis remain outside the proved scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Unconditional results are the normal--affine algebra, operator perturbation, the positive finite regular witness, the singular branch witness, the transverse four-level witness, strict single-pair nonattainment, and the explicit outcome-only selected-parameter comparison. The general quotient formula is only a conditional Hilbert conclusion under reverse lifting and bridge-score pathwise validity. The general primitive learned-projection, regularity, efficiency-attainment, variance-ratio, and Wald theorems remain open. The observed bridge functional receives a causal ATE interpretation only from the separate latent identification proposition. No efficiency claim is made for arbitrary path-poor subcharts, rank-changing unions, generic compact ill-posed operators, or an external outcome-only model whose neighboring-law parameter has not been imported.
